page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / So long Denise!
title: So long Denise!
topic: Language for helping others with advice about their career
description:
It's Denise's last day working at Tip Top Trading. Anna is busy trying to get everyone to sign her leaving card, but Denise is quite worried about the future. Hopefully Anna can help her with some good careers advice!
This episode focuses on the language that you might use to try and help someone find another job.
phrases: Try looking in the job section in the newspaper.
There are loads of job-finding websites you could sign up for.
What about ringing some of the people you know?
You could register with a recruitment agency.

listening_challenge.question: What does Denise get for her leaving present?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello again. It's a difficult day at the offices of Tip Top Trading. The office assistant Denise is losing her job, and today is her last day. Anna is busy with her work and trying to get everyone to sign Denise's leaving card.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Paul, have you signed Denise's leaving card yet?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: No, not yet. Have you got a pen? "Sorry to see you go. Best foot forward. Paul." There. I feel a bit guilty, it was me who got rid of her.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah. Well, you should feel really bad. I can't believe you're getting rid of her.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom, do you want to sign the card?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, of course. "You are…were…the best employee we ever had. So sad to see you go. Kiss, kiss, kiss. Tom."

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Gosh. Three kisses! Erm, you haven't given me any money for her leaving present yet, have you?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh sorry, a bit of a cash flow problem… Here, have a pound.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: That's generous!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh crumbs, she's crying again. Anna, could you deal with her? I've got something important to do.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh yeah. Me too.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Denise, are you OK? Are you upset about leaving?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes. I've loved working here. I've made some good friends… like you Anna… Oh, and being able to make free phone calls has been good.  What am I going to do now?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh dear Anna. It sounds like Denise needs some career advice.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Career advice?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: She needs some guidance on what to do next and where to find another job. What would you do in her situation?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Look in the newspaper, ring my contacts, register with a job agency?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Exactly! I'm sure you can give her some good advice. Go on, give it a go!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK, I'll try. Cheer up Denise, you need to think positively.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Do I? I'm unemployed from tomorrow, how am I ever going to find another job?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, have you tried looking in the job section of the newspaper?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It's a good place to start. And there are loads of job-finding websites you could sign up for.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I don't have a computer.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well what about ringing some of the people you know; contacts who may know about a job.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hmm, I hadn't thought about that.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: And of course, you could register with a recruitment agency. They're good at finding jobs for you.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh, that's a good idea. Anna, you're brilliant! What great ideas… you're so kind and… thoughtful.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Anna could you… Oh no, she's crying again.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh no, shall we go back into your office Paul?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No, no. It's OK, Denise is crying with happiness. She's feeling better now.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh well, in that case… shall we all gather round and officially say goodbye to Denise.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: It's an emotional day for Denise, but Anna has been really useful with her career advice. If a professional career advisor is not available, giving some of your own advice can sometimes be useful. Let's hear again what Anna suggested…
You need to think positively.
Try looking in the job section of the newspaper.
There are loads of job-finding websites you could sign up for.
What about ringing some of the people you know?
You could register with a recruitment agency.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: OK everyone, the time has come to say farewell to Denise. It's with regret we've had to let her go.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: We? You, Paul.

transcript.speaker: Pau
transcript.text: Thank you for all your hard work and we wish you very well in the future.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Anna, I think we have a gift for Denise?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: There you go Denise. Careful, it's quite heavy.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh, what a beautiful fruit bowl… and full of plastic fruit!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I'll get it. Sorry about that everyone. That was a company called Nice'n'Cheesy, they remember you Anna. They liked your sales pitch and want to order a hundred thousand plastic grapes to go with their cheeses!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: What?! Brilliant! Ooops.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: My new fruit bowl!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh dear. Poor Denise! It looks like she might be leaving the company at just the wrong time. I wonder if she'll be back? You'll have to join us again for the next episode of English at Work. Bye!
